@rprouse: Since this really is a critical error, let me know if you don't have time to work it right now and I'll do an interim fix for the alpha-1 release. Meanwhile, some ideas...

Looking at the code in nunit-console ResultReporter.cs, I see that I put a // TODO there indicating that we need to report setup and  teardown tests. The nunitlite runner ResultReporter has the same problem, although it's not commented. Both classes only report suite failures when the suite is a Theory.

NUnit 2.6 reported failures in TestFixtureSetUp and TestFixtureTearDown by checking the FailureSite property of the result, which indicated whether a failure occured in SetUp, TearDown, etc. There is no corresponding property in the XML for NUnit 3.0.

A short term solution would be to report any suite failures or errors if there is a message other than "One or more child tests had errors". This is pretty ugly, but could work in the short term.

Any permanent solution requires adding some info to the result that is delivered to nunit-console. We could re-introduce FailureSite, but I'd prefer to try to do  without it. Perhaps the easiest would be to distinguish teardown failures by the result state. We could have Failed:TearDown for example. Alternatively, we could have a special state for a suite that failed because some child failed, like
Failed:ChildFailure. Any of these require changes all through the framework, so they may be better to introduce later.

@CharliePoole, I might be able to look at this tonight, but if I don't get
it then, I won't have much time until Friday.

## 

Rob Prouse

I welcome VSRE emails. Learn more at http://vsre.info/

A further issue we should deal with: NUnit has historically treated any
Assertion
failrue in TearDown or TestFixtureTearDown as an error, rather than a
failure,
because Asserts are not supposed to be in teardowns. So what you get is an
exception error message.

I can see that you needed to put your asserts in the teardown in order to
test
what you were trying to test. I've done the same myself. So long as we think
this is only needed when testing NUnit itself, I think we can live with
treating
it this way. If we think it's more generally useful, then we may need to
change.

Charlie

issue.title: Different test runners show different results for NUnit.Framework.TestContextOneTimeTearDownTests
issue.body:
Accidentally I've found that `TestContextOneTimeTearDownTests` test fixture behaves differently depending on which test runner is used. Here below I am referencing to the following source code, especially `OneTimeTearDown` method.
https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/5c4394af96570afb559f7bce238aa859b9ad0c61/src/NUnitFramework/tests/TestContextTests.cs#L452-L486

# Steps To Reproduce

1. If you are running tests from IDE, set a breakpoint 🔴 in `OneTimeTearDown` method.
2. Run `TestContextOneTimeTearDownTests` test fixture as a whole in `nunit.framework` test assembly, but not each test separately.

# Actual Result
## ReSharper
_The version of ReSharper is 2018.1.2._
**❌ `TestContextOneTimeTearDownTests` failed.**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22633878/41839375-c57ef6e2-786b-11e8-83bf-82e32d6e2d8c.png)
- `context.Result.PassCount` = 2
- `context.Result.SkipCount` = 0 _(the reason of failure)_

## Visual Studio
**✔️ Tests are passed.**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22633878/41841297-96d40e18-7870-11e8-83ba-ec95343d2800.png)
- `context.Result.PassCount` = 3
- `context.Result.SkipCount` = 0

`Assert.That(context.Result.PassCount, Is.EqualTo(2));` actually throws `AssertionException`, but seems it isn't counted by VS, because all is green.

## NUnit Console
**✔️ Tests are passed.**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22633878/41841462-fe5862e6-7870-11e8-8307-e9d0cd8098bb.png)
- Passed: 2
- Skipped: 1

# Expected Result
Since all 3 test runners provide different results, I am not sure what is correct. It depends on how "Explicit" tests and "TearDown" failures should be treated.
